name: HivePunk 632
subject: Hugging Face Datasets viewer configuration
thesis: Viewer configuration is primarily file-to-split mapping plus declarative metadata, but its limits mean successful configuration does not guarantee a complete preview for large datasets. The documented 5GB and 100-row constraints should shape expectations for any published dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: There are no constraints on how to structure dataset repositories.
claims.quote: There are no constraints on how to structure dataset repositories.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Splits are automatically detected based on file and directory names.
claims.quote: Splits are automatically detected based on file and directory names.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Manual configuration can choose data files to show in the Dataset Viewer using YAML.
claims.quote: You can choose the data files to show in the Dataset Viewer for your dataset using YAML.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A subset is also called a configuration and is a sub-dataset contained within a larger dataset.
claims.quote: A subset (also called configuration ) is a sub-dataset contained within a larger dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: DatasetInfo config_name is the name of the configuration derived from BuilderConfig.
claims.quote: config_name ( str , optional ) — The name of the configuration derived from BuilderConfig .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: DatasetInfo features specify the dataset column types.
claims.quote: features ( Features , optional ) — The features used to specify the dataset’s column types.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: DatasetInfo splits is the mapping between split name and metadata.
claims.quote: splits ( dict , optional ) — The mapping between split name and metadata.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Dataset pages include a table arranged by pages of 100 rows.
claims.quote: Each dataset page includes a table with the contents of the dataset, arranged by pages of 100 rows.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The rows API slice length has a maximum of 100.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Depending on format, the Dataset Viewer may only show the first 5GB of a dataset.
claims.quote: The Dataset Viewer supports large scale datasets, but depending on the data format it may only show the first 5GB of the dataset:

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: TooBigContentError means the dataset viewer could not read a preview within its limits.
claims.quote: If you see Error code: TooBigContentError , then the dataset viewer could not read a preview within its limits.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Configuration can be done either automatically by file naming or manually via YAML assigning files to splits/subsets.
claims.math: c2 states automatic detection; c3 states manual YAML choice; together they imply both routes exist.

risks: Viewer may only show first 5GB depending on format, so preview may be partial for large datasets.
TooBigContentError can occur when preview cannot be read within limits, especially with large first-row values.
Manual configuration errors can cause wrong files to be assigned to splits or subsets.
Features, config_name and splits metadata may be absent or not confirmable for a given dataset from the pages read.
Gated or private datasets require a user token, so unauthenticated API access may fail.
wouldChangeMind: Finding official numeric TooBigContentError limits that contradict the partial-preview risk assessment.
Finding a complete YAML schema showing additional required viewer configuration fields.
Finding evidence that 5GB limits no longer apply to the formats documented as limited.
